name: Saul of Tarsus
charge: Persecuting the church; consenting to Stephen’s death; compelling the saints to blaspheme
summary: The witnesses who stoned Stephen laid their clothes at his feet, and he was consenting to the death; from that day he made havock of the congregation, entering every house and committing men and women to prison (Acts 7:58; Acts 8:1-3). Breathing out threatenings and slaughter, he went to the high priest for letters to Damascus so that he might bring any he found of that way bound to Jerusalem (Acts 9:1-2). A light out of heaven struck him down on the road, and the voice asked why he was persecuting Christ; the man who came to lead others bound was led by the hand into the city, blind, and afterward was told he was a chosen vessel who would suffer for that name (Acts 9:3-9; Acts 9:15-16).
offenseFull: The witnesses who stoned Stephen laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, and he was consenting to his death (Acts 7:58; Acts 8:1). From that day he made havock of the congregation, entering into every house and haling men and women and committing them to prison (Acts 8:3). Still breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples, he went to the high priest and asked for letters to the synagogues at Damascus, so that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem (Acts 9:1-2). Before the followers of Christ were called Christians at Antioch they were called this way, after the one who said he is the way (John 14:6). Authority from the chief priests gave the campaign an official face. It did not make it obedience to God.

His own account is heavier than Luke’s summary. He persecuted this way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women (Acts 22:4-5). He shut up many of the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them often in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, and being exceedingly mad against them, persecuted them even to strange cities (Acts 26:9-11). He thought he ought to do it. He had been brought up at the feet of Gamaliel and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers (Acts 22:3); he was of the stock of Israel and the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews, a Pharisee, and by his own reckoning blameless touching the righteousness which is in the law (Philippians 3:5-6); and he profited in that religion above many of his equals, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of his fathers, while he wasted the church of God beyond measure (Galatians 1:13-14). Learning, zeal and certainty did not keep him out of the gravest sin.
judgmentFull: As he came near Damascus a light from heaven shined round about him, he fell to the earth and heard a voice asking why he was persecuting him (Acts 9:3-5). Christ was already dead at that time, and the question still stands in the present tense, because what is done to one of his little ones is done to him. Trembling and astonished, the man who had set out to lead others bound asked what he would have him do, and was led by the hand into the city, and was three days without sight and neither ate nor drank (Acts 9:6-9). The men with him stood speechless, hearing a voice and seeing no man, while his own retelling says they saw the light and heard

not the voice, the other half of one event and no contradiction (Acts 22:9). Ananias objected that he had heard by many how much evil this man had done to the saints at Jerusalem, and was told to go, for he was a chosen vessel to bear the name before the Gentiles and kings and the children of Israel, and would be shown how great things he must suffer for it (Acts 9:13-16). Ananias went in, called him Brother Saul, and there fell from his eyes as it had been scales, and he received sight and was baptized (Acts 9:17-18).

He did it in ignorance, which is why the scripture says to judge nothing before the time (1 Corinthians 4:5). The things any of us did before this truth were worthy of death, so no man is written off as beyond repentance, and the enemies who can still repent are the ones inside our own nation (Romans 11:28). Straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, and all that heard him were amazed and asked whether this was not the man who destroyed them which called on that name; but he increased the more in strength and confounded the Jews at Damascus (Acts 9:20-22). The mercy did not cancel the cost. They took counsel to kill him and watched the gates day and night, and the disciples took him by night and let him down the wall in a basket (Acts 9:23-25). He afterward called himself the least of the apostles, not meet to be called an apostle, because he persecuted the church of God (1 Corinthians 15:9), and a blasphemer and a persecutor and injurious, who obtained mercy because he did it ignorantly in unbelief, and was set forth as a pattern of Christ’s longsuffering to them which should believe after (1 Timothy 1:12-16). The gospel he preached was not taught him by any man; he had it by revelation, went into Arabia, and only after three years went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and James (Galatians 1:11-12; Galatians 1:17-19).

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Cursing or blasphemy against God forbidden.
We should give no occasion for blasphemy to occur.
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.

text.text: And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man’s feet, whose name was Saul.

And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison.
And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,
And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.
Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.

I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;
Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.
For ye have heard of my conversation in time past in the Jews’ religion, how that beyond measure I persecuted the church of God, and wasted it:
And profited in the Jews’ religion above many my equals in mine own nation, being more exceedingly zealous of the traditions of my fathers.
And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:
And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.
And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.
And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem:
And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name.
But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:
For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.
And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.
As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers’ sakes.
And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests?
But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.
And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him:
But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.
Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.
For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;
Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord was exceeding abundant with faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.
This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
Howbeit for this cause I obtained mercy, that in me first Jesus Christ might shew forth all longsuffering, for a pattern to them which should hereafter believe on him to life everlasting.
But I certify you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached of me is not after man.
For I neither received it of man, neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ.
Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.
Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to see Peter, and abode with him fifteen days.
But other of the apostles saw I none, save James the Lord’s brother.
